source_text: CUM moneat Dominus et dicat: Vos estis sal terrae, cumque esse nos jubeat ad innocentiam simplices, et tamen cum simplicitate prudentes, quid aliud, fratres dilectissimi, quam providere nos convenit, et sollicito corde vigilantes, subdoli hostis insidias intelligere pariter et cavere ne qui Christum sapientiam Dei Patris induimus, minus sapere in tuenda salute videamur? Neque enim persecutio sola metuenda est et ea quae subruendis ac dejiciendis Dei servis aperta impugnatione grassantur. Facilior cautio est ubi manifesta formido est, et ad certamen animus ante praestruitur quando se adversarius confitetur. Plus metuendus est et cavendus inimicus cum latenter obrepit, cum, per pacis imaginem fallens, occultis accessibus serpit; unde et nomen serpentis accepit. Ea est ejus semper astutia, ea est circumveniendi hominis caeca et latebrosa fallacia. Sic ab initio statim mundi fefellit, et, verbis mendacibus blandiens, rudes animas incauta credulitate decepit. Dominum ipsum tentare conatus, quasi obreperet rursus et falleret, latenter accessit. Intellectus tamen est et retusus; et ideo prostratus, quia agnitus atque detectus. Unde nobis exemplum datum est veteris hominis viam fugere, vestigiis Christi viventis insistere; ne denuo incauti in mortis laqueum revolvamur, sed, ad periculum providi, accepta immortalitate potiamur. Immortalitate autem potiri quomodo possumus, nisi ea quibus mors expugnatur et vincitur, Christi mandata servemus, ipso monente et dicente: Si vis ad vitam venire, serva mandata. Et iterum: Si feceritis quae mando vobis, jam non dico vos servos, sed amicos. Hos denique fortes dicit et stabiles, hos super petram robusta mole fundatos, hos contra omnes tempestates et turbines saeculi immobili et inconcussa firmitate solidatos. Qui audit, inquit, verba mea et facit ea, similabo eum viro sapienti qui aedificavit domum suam supra petram. Descendit pluvia, venerunt flumina, flaverunt venti et impegerunt in domum illam, et non cecidit; fundata enim fuit super petram. Verbis igitur ejus insistere, quaecumque et docuit et fecit discere et facere debemus. Caeterum credere se in Christum, quomodo dicit qui non facit quod Christus facere praecepit? Aut unde perveniet ad praemium fidei, qui fidem non vult servare mandati? Nutet necesse est et vagetur, et, spiritu erroris abreptus, velut pulvis quem ventus excutit ventiletur; nec ambulando proficiet ad salutem, qui salutaris viae non tenet veritatem. Cavenda sunt autem, fratres dilectissimi, non solum quae sunt aperta atque manifesta, sed et astutae fraudis subtilitate fallentia. Quid vero astutius, quidve subtilius, quam ut Christi adventu detectus ac prostratus inimicus, postquam lux Gentibus venit et sospitandis hominibus salutare lumen effulsit, ut surdi auditum gratiae spiritalis admitterent, aperirent ad Deum oculos suos caeci, infirmi aeterna sanitate revalescerent, claudi ad Ecclesiam currerent, muti claris vocibus et precibus orarent, videns ille idola derelicta et per nimium credentium populum sedes suas ac templa deserta, excogitaverit novam fraudem, ut sub ipso christiani nominis titulo fallat incautos? Haereses invenit et schismata, quibus subverteret fidem, veritatem corrumperet, scinderet unitatem. Quos detinere non potest in viae veteris caecitate, circumscribit et decipit novi itineris errore. Rapit de ipsa Ecclesia homines; et, dum sibi appropinquasse jam lumini atque evasisse saeculi noctem videntur, alias nescientibus tenebras rursus infundit, ut cum Evangelio Christi et cum observatione ejus et lege non stantes, Christianos se vocent, et ambulantes in tenebris habere se lumen existiment, blandiente adversario atque fallente, qui, secundum Apostoli vocem, transfigurat se velut angelum lucis, et ministros suos subornat velut ministros justitiae, asserentes noctem pro die, interitum pro salute, desperationem sub obtentu spei, perfidiam sub praetextu fidei, antichristum sub vocabulo Christi; ut, dum verisimilia mentiuntur, veritatem subtilitate frustrentur. Hoc eo fit, fratres dilectissimi, dum ad veritatis originem non reditur, nec caput quaeritur, nec magistri coelestis doctrina servatur. Quae si quis consideret et examinet, tractatu longo atque argumentis opus non est. Probatio est ad fidem facilis compendio veritatis. Loquitur Dominus ad Petrum: Ego tibi dico, inquit, quia tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram aedificabo Ecclesiam meam, et portae inferorum non vincent eam. Et tibi dabo claves regni coelorum: et quae ligaveris super terram, erunt ligata et in coelis; et quaecumque solveris super terram, erunt soluta et in coelis. Et iterum eidem post resurrectionem suam dicit: Pasce oves meas. Super illum unum aedificat Ecclesiam suam, et illi pascendas mandat oves suas. Et quamvis Apostolis omnibus post resurrectionem suam parem potestatem tribuat et dicat, Sicut misit me Pater, et ego mitto vos: accipite Spiritum sanctum; si cujus remiseritis peccata, remittentur illi, si cujus tenueritis, tenebuntur, tamen, ut unitatem manifestaret, unam cathedram constituit, unitatis ejusdem originem ab uno incipientem sua auctoritate disposuit. Hoc erant utique et caeteri Apostoli quod fuit Petrus, pari consortio praediti et honoris et potestatis, sed exordium ab unitate proficiscitur, et primatus Petro datur, ut una Christi Ecclesia et cathedra una monstretur. Et pastores sunt omnes, et grex unus ostenditur, qui ab Apostolis omnibus unanimi consensione pascatur, ut Ecclesia Christi una monstretur. Quam unam Ecclesiam etiam in Cantico canticorum Spiritus sanctus ex persona Domini designat et dicit: Una est columba mea, perfecta mea, una est matri suae, electa genitrici suae. Hanc Ecclesiae unitiatem qui non tenet, tenere se fidem credit? Qui Ecclesiae renititur et resistit, qui cathedram Petri, super quem fundata est Ecclesia, deserit, in Ecclesia se esse confidit? quando et beatus apostolus Paulus hoc idem doceat et sacramentum unitatis ostendat dicens: Unum corpus et unus spiritus, una spes vocationis vestrae, unus Dominus, una fides, unum Baptisma, unus Deus.
pass_a_gloss: When the Lord warns and says: You are the salt of the earth, and when He commands us to be simple in innocence, and yet prudent with simplicity, what else, most beloved brothers, is fitting for us to do, than to provide for ourselves, and with a solicitous heart, watching, to understand and beware of the insidious plots of the cunning enemy, lest we, who have put on Christ, the wisdom of God the Father, seem to be less wise in guarding our salvation? For it is not only persecution that is to be feared, and those things that openly attack and overthrow the servants of God. Caution is easier where there is open fear, and the mind is prepared for battle when the adversary confesses himself. The enemy is more to be feared and avoided when he creeps in secretly, when, deceiving by the image of peace, he slips in with hidden approaches; whence he has also received the name of serpent. This is always his cunning, this is the blind and hidden deceit of circumventing man. Thus from the beginning of the world he deceived, and, flattering with lying words, he deceived the simple souls with unsuspecting credulity. He even tried to tempt the Lord Himself, and, as if he would creep in again and deceive, he approached secretly. However, he was understood and repelled; and therefore he was prostrated, because he was recognized and detected. Whence an example has been given to us to flee the way of the old man, to follow in the footsteps of the living Christ; lest, being unguarded, we again fall into the snare of death, but, providing for danger, we may possess immortality. But how can we possess immortality, unless we keep the commandments of Christ, by which death is overcome and conquered, He Himself warning and saying: If you wish to come to life, keep the commandments. And again: If you do what I command you, I will no longer call you servants, but friends. These, finally, He calls strong and stable, founded on a strong rock, solidified with immovable and unshakable firmness against all the tempests and whirlwinds of the world. He who hears, He says, my words and does them, I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on a rock. The rain came down, the rivers came, the winds blew and struck that house, and it did not fall; for it was founded on a rock. Therefore, we must insist on His words, and do what He has taught and commanded us to do and learn. But how can one believe himself to be in Christ, who does not do what Christ commanded? Or how will he come to the reward of faith, who does not wish to keep the faith of the commandment? It is necessary for him to waver and wander, and, seized by the spirit of error, to be blown about like dust which the wind blows; nor will he make progress towards salvation, who does not hold to the truth of the salutary way. But we must beware, most beloved brothers, not only of open and manifest things, but also of the subtle deceit of cunning. What, indeed, is more cunning, or what more subtle, than that the enemy, detected and prostrated by the advent of Christ, after the light of the Gentiles has come and the salutary light has shone for the salvation of men, so that the deaf might receive the hearing of spiritual grace, the blind might open their eyes to God, the weak might be strengthened by eternal health, the lame might run to the Church, the mute might pray with clear voices and prayers, seeing that idols are abandoned and his seats and temples are deserted by the multitude of believers, has devised a new deceit, that he might deceive the unguarded under the very title of the Christian name? He has invented heresies and schisms, by which he might subvert the faith, corrupt the truth, and divide the unity. Those whom he cannot detain in the blindness of the old way, he surrounds and deceives with the error of the new way. He snatches men from the very Church; and while they seem to have approached the light and escaped the night of the world, he pours in other darknesses, unknown to them, so that, not standing with the Gospel of Christ, and with His observation and law, they call themselves Christians, and, walking in darkness, think they have the light, the adversary flattering and deceiving, who, according to the voice of the Apostle, transforms himself into an angel of light, and his ministers as ministers of justice, asserting night for day, destruction for salvation, despair under the pretext of hope, perfidy under the pretext of faith, antichrist under the name of Christ; so that, while they speak what is plausible, they may frustrate the truth with subtlety. This happens, most beloved brothers, when one does not return to the origin of truth, nor seek the head, nor preserve the doctrine of the heavenly Master. If anyone considers and examines this, there is no need for a long discussion or arguments. The proof is easy, a compendium of truth. The Lord speaks to Peter: I say to you, He says, that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell will not prevail against it. And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven. And again to him after His resurrection He says: Feed my sheep. He builds His Church on him alone, and commands him to feed His sheep. And although He gives equal power to all the Apostles after His resurrection, and says: As the Father has sent me, I also send you; receive the Holy Spirit; if you forgive the sins of anyone, they will be forgiven; if you retain the sins of anyone, they will be retained, yet, to manifest unity, He establishes one chair, and with His authority, He arranges the origin of unity, beginning from one. This, indeed, were also the other Apostles, what Peter was, endowed with equal partnership and honor and power, but the beginning proceeds from unity, and the primacy is given to Peter, that one Church of Christ and one chair may be shown. And all are shepherds, and one flock is shown, which is fed by all the Apostles with unanimous consent, that the one Church of Christ may be shown. Which one Church the Holy Spirit also designates in the Song of Songs, speaking in the person of the Lord, and says: My dove is one, my perfect one, one to her mother, chosen by her parent. Who does not hold to this unity of the Church, believes himself to hold to the faith? Who resists and opposes the Church, who deserts the chair of Peter, on which the Church is founded, confides in being in the Church? When also the blessed Apostle Paul teaches this same thing, and shows the sacrament of unity, saying: One body and one spirit, one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one Baptism, one God.

pass_b_english: When the Lord warns us and says, "You are the salt of the earth" (Matt 5:13), and commands us to be simple in innocence yet prudent with that simplicity, what else should we do, beloved brothers, but take care? With watchful, anxious hearts we must discern and guard against the cunning enemy's hidden plots, lest we who have put on Christ, the wisdom of God the Father, appear less wise in protecting our own salvation. It is not only open persecution we must fear, the kind that attacks and overthrows God's servants openly. Caution comes easily when danger is plain, and the mind readies itself for battle when the adversary shows himself. The enemy is far more dangerous and to be avoided when he creeps in secretly, deceiving under the guise of peace and slipping in by hidden approaches; that is why he is called the serpent. This has always been his cunning, his blind and concealed deceit in circumventing humanity. From the very beginning of the world he deceived, flattering with lying words and trapping simple souls through their unsuspecting credulity. He even attempted to tempt the Lord Himself, approaching secretly as if to creep in and deceive again. But he was recognized and repelled, and so he fell prostrate because he was detected. From this we are given an example: we must flee the way of the old man and walk in the footsteps of the living Christ, so that we do not fall unawares once more into the snare of death, but, foreseeing the danger, may take hold of immortality. And how can we possess immortality unless we keep the commandments of Christ, by which death is overcome and conquered? He Himself warns and says: "If you wish to enter life, keep the commandments" (Matt 19:17). And again: "If you do what I command you, I no longer call you servants, but friends" (John 15:14). These He calls strong and stable, founded on a massive rock, solidified with immovable and unshakable firmness against all the tempests and whirlwinds of the age. "Whoever hears my words and does them," He says, "I will compare him to a wise man who built his house on the rock. The rain fell, the floods came, the winds blew and beat against that house, and it did not fall, because it had been founded on the rock" (Matt 7:24-25). Therefore we must stand firm on His words, and learn to do everything He taught and commanded. But how can someone believe he is in Christ if he does not do what Christ commanded? Or how will he reach the reward of faith if he refuses to keep the faith of the commandment? Such a person must waver and wander, seized by a spirit of error and blown about like dust before the wind; he will make no progress toward salvation, because he does not hold to the truth of the saving way. Yet, beloved brothers, we must beware not only of what is open and manifest, but also of what deceives through the subtle cunning of fraud. What could be more cunning or subtle than this: the enemy, detected and prostrated by the advent of Christ, after the light came to the Gentiles and the saving light shone for humanity so that the deaf might receive the hearing of spiritual grace, the blind open their eyes to God, the weak recover through eternal health, the lame run to the Church, and the mute pray with clear voices, seeing that idols were abandoned and his seats and temples deserted by the multitude of believers, he devises a new deceit to trap the unwary under the very title of the Christian name? He invents heresies and schisms to subvert the faith, corrupt the truth, and divide the unity. Those he cannot hold in the blindness of the old way, he ensnares through the error of a new way. He snatches men from the very Church; and while they think they have approached the light and escaped the night of the world, he pours in another darkness, unknown to them, so that, not standing with the Gospel of Christ and His observance and law, they call themselves Christians, and walking in darkness, imagine they have the light. The adversary flatters and deceives, transforming himself, as the Apostle says, into an angel of light, and his ministers into ministers of righteousness (2 Cor 11:14-15), calling night day, destruction salvation, despair under the pretext of hope, perfidy under the pretext of faith, antichrist under the name of Christ, so that by speaking plausible things they may frustrate the truth through subtlety. This happens, beloved brothers, when we do not return to the origin of truth, nor seek the head, nor keep the doctrine of the heavenly Master. If anyone considers and examines this, there is no need for lengthy discussion or arguments. The proof is easy, a compendium of truth. The Lord speaks to Peter: "I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell will not prevail against it. And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven" (Matt 16:18-19). And again, after His resurrection, He says to him: "Feed my sheep" (John 21:17). He builds His Church on him alone, and commands him to feed His sheep. And although He grants equal power to all the Apostles after His resurrection, saying, "As the Father has sent me, even so I send you. Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven; if you retain the sins of any, they are retained" (John 20:21-23), yet, to manifest unity, He establishes one chair, and by His authority arranges the origin of that unity to proceed from one. The other Apostles were indeed what Peter was, endowed with equal partnership of honor and power, but the beginning proceeds from unity, and primacy is given to Peter, so that one Church of Christ and one chair may be shown. And all are shepherds, and one flock is shown, which is fed by all the Apostles with unanimous consent, so that the one Church of Christ may be shown. The Holy Spirit also designates this one Church in the Song of Songs, speaking in the person of the Lord: "My dove is one, my perfect one, she is the only one of her mother, chosen by her who bore her" (Song 6:9). Who does not hold this unity of the Church believes he holds the faith? Who resists and opposes the Church, who deserts the chair of Peter on which the Church is founded, trusts that he is in the Church? Especially when the blessed Apostle Paul teaches this same thing and displays the sacrament of unity, saying: "One body and one Spirit, one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God" (Eph 4:4-6).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text, including the complex theological arguments regarding the unity of the Church and the primacy of Peter. All scripture citations in Pass B (Matt 5:13, Matt 19:17, John 15:14, Matt 7:24-25, 2 Cor 11:14-15, Matt 16:18-19, John 21:17, John 20:21-23, Song 6:9, Eph 4:4-6) correctly identify the source material alluded to in the Latin. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source.
